بَلْبَلَةٌ inf. n. of بَلْبَلَ [q. v.]. (M, K.) ＝
-A2- A state of confusion, or mixture, of tongues, or languages. (M, K. *) In the copies of the K, الأَسِنَّة is here erroneously put for الأَلْسِنَة. (TA.) ―
-b2- Also, and ↓ بَلْبَالٌ , The vain, or unprofitable, or evil, suggestion of anxieties in the bosom: (T:) or anxiety, and vain, or unprofitable, or evil, suggestion of the mind: (S:) or intense anxiety, and vain, or unprofitable, or evil, suggestions or thoughts; (M, K;) as also ↓ بُلَابِلٌ , (so in the M, accord. to the TT,) or ↓ بَلَابِلُ : (so in copies of the K:) this last [however] is pl. of ↓ بَلْبَالٌ ; (T;) which also signifies vehement distress in the bosom; (M, K;) and so does ↓ بَلْبَالَةٌ : (IJ, M:) or ↓ بَلْبَالٌ signifies anxiety and grief: and, as also بَلْبَلَةٌ, a motion, or commotion, in the heart, arising from grief or love. (Har p. 94.)
From An Arabic-English Lexicon (Edward William Lane)
